time-duration-calculator.formula:
Difference:
minutes = (endH x 60 + endM) - (startH x 60 + startM)
if minutes < 0: minutes += 1440 (end is next day)
hours = floor(minutes / 60), mins = minutes mod 60

Add / Subtract:
totalSeconds = startSeconds ± (h x 3600 + m x 60 + s)
dayOffset = floor(totalSeconds / 86400)
clockTime = totalSeconds mod 86400 (wrapped into 0–86399)
howTo: Pick Difference to measure between two times, or Add/Subtract to shift one time.
Enter the times with the time pickers (24-hour clock).
For Add/Subtract, choose + or − and type the hours, minutes, and seconds.
Read the result instantly — duration, totals, and any day rollover are all shown.
Use the totals for timesheets; copy the numbers straight into your records.
keyFacts: Time arithmetic is base-60, not base-100: 90 minutes is 1 hour 30 minutes, never 1.9 hours.
If the end time is earlier than the start time, the tool assumes the end falls on the next day — 22:00 to 06:00 is an 8-hour night shift.
Adding time can roll past midnight; the tool shows the resulting clock time plus how many days forward or back you landed.
All results also appear as total minutes and total seconds, which payroll and billing systems usually want.
Times are plain clock readings — the tool does not apply timezones or daylight saving.
